title: Degree of Q(n-th root of p): minimal polynomial X^n - p via Eisenstein

problemStatement.formal: For prime p and n >= 1, X^n - p is the minimal polynomial over Q of the real n-th root p^{1/n}; hence [Q(p^{1/n}) : Q] = n.
problemStatement.plain: Eisenstein's criterion already gives that X^n - p is irreducible over Q for every prime p and every exponent n. This problem draws the standard field-theoretic consequence: since X^n - p is monic, irreducible, and vanishes at p^{1/n}, it must be the minimal polynomial of p^{1/n} over Q, so the extension Q(p^{1/n})/Q has degree exactly n. Eisenstein thus produces an algebraic number of every prescribed degree.
whyMatters: Bridges the gallery's irreducibility of X^n - p to the textbook corollary [Q(p^{1/n}):Q] = n, which the gallery has not yet formalized.
Gives an explicit uniform construction of algebraic numbers of arbitrarily large prescribed degree, foundational for Galois theory and field-tower computations.

proven: X^n - p is irreducible over Z (gallery eisenstein-criterion-oq-01, irreducible_X_pow_sub_C_prime).
Mathlib minimal-polynomial and field-degree API: minpoly, AdjoinRoot.powerBasis, IntermediateField.adjoin.finrank.
open: No gallery entry states minpoly_Q(p^{1/n}) = X^n - p for general prime p and general n.
No gallery entry states [Q(p^{1/n}):Q] = n for the general family (only the concrete cube-root-of-3 irrationality case exists).
knownResults.goal: Formalize in Lean 4, on top of the gallery Eisenstein entry and Mathlib, that X^n - p is the minimal polynomial over Q of p^{1/n} (prime p, n >= 1), and derive [Q(p^{1/n}):Q] = n, including at least one concrete instance such as [Q(sqrt 2):Q] = 2 or [Q(cbrt 2):Q] = 3.
